summary: Approval request: sampled anonymized customer output dump for privacy audit of new inference caching behavior
description:
Issue summary: Internal Privacy & Product Analytics teams request a sampled export of inference outputs tied to recent cache hits to validate the new prefix caching behavior introduced last week.

Rationale: Audit needs to assess whether cached responses can leak user-provided PII when prefix reuse occurs across similar prompts. Product wants to correlate cache-hit patterns with prompt templates to decide whether to increase prefix isolation.

Request owner: Product Analytics (internal). Compliance owner: Privacy Engineering.
request_details: We request a sampled dataset consisting of 5,000 inference output records from production spanning 2026-03-04 to 2026-03-10, filtered to requests that had a cache hit (cache_key != null) and sequence length <= 2048. Export must include minimal metadata: timestamp, model_version, route_id, cache_hit_flag, prompt_template_hash, and the generated output text. All customer identifiers must be removed or salted. Export format: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) with one record per line.
impact: Low risk to availability but moderate privacy sensitivity. Data will contain free-form generated text potentially containing customer PII. This is an internal audit only; no external sharing. Delay in approval blocks the product decision on cache isolation, which could cause a conservative rollback and increased cost if not completed within two weeks.
redaction_strategy: 1) Remove all explicit customer identifiers (user_id, account_id) before export. 2) Apply automated PII redaction pass using the company's PII-detection model (version pii-detector-v3). 3) Apply token-level masking for email patterns, IP addresses, and API keys. 4) For remaining ambiguous spans, apply hashing with per-audit salt and record a mapping only in the secure compliance vault. 5) Maintain an audit log of redaction steps and operator who ran them.
audit_plan:
1) Compliance will review and approve the redaction pipeline on a staging sample (50 records) prior to full export.
2) Redaction will be executed on a dedicated ephemeral job in the privacy enclave.
3) Resulting dataset will be stored in encrypted S3 with restricted ACLs for 30 days.
4) Product Analytics access will be via temporary role with MFA and session recording.
5) After 30 days, dataset will be securely deleted and deletion verified by Compliance.
retention_exemption_request: Retention limited to 30 days for audit; request explicit approval for this short-term retention window. No permanent storage requested.
